catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET 10 - FIRST READING (image only, unverified)

EXPOSURE / RULES STATEMENT
Nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification of any work or author for these pieces, and I do not offer one. I opened only PROMPT.md and the 48 image files. One thing beyond the bare rules: I ran a file listing of the packet directory to learn the image names and pixel sizes (this showed the name packet.json, which I did not open), and I kept private working notes in a scratch file while reading. No web, search, catalogue or edition was used.

HOW THE PACKET IS ORGANISED (from the images)
Six separate parchment pieces, each with two faces. Faces are labelled "A"/"B" only by order of appearance; I cannot say which is recto.
  Piece 1: image-001 (overview, face A), image-002 (top tile), image-003 (bottom tile); image-004 (overview, face B), image-005 (top), image-006 (bottom).
  Piece 2: image-007 (overview, face A), image-008..011 (tiles TL, TR, BL, BR); image-012 (overview, face B), image-013..016 (TL, TR, BL, BR).
  Piece 3: image-017 (overview, face A), image-018 (top), image-019 (bottom); image-020 (overview, face B), image-021, image-022.
  Piece 4: image-023 (overview, face A), image-024 (top), image-025 (bottom); image-026 (overview, face B), image-027 (top), image-028 (bottom).
  Piece 5: image-029 (overview, face A), image-030..033 (TL, TR, BL, BR); image-034 (overview, face B), image-035..038.
  Piece 6: image-039 (overview, face A), image-040..043 (TL, TR, BL, BR); image-044 (overview, face B), image-045..048.
Tiles overlap their neighbours; where a line appears in two tiles I give it once and note the repeat.

GENERAL LAYOUT SURVEY (observation)
All six are small, worm-eaten binding scraps on a black background. None preserves a full column width, a running title or a folio number. Two sizes of script recur: a larger, upright gothic book hand, and a much smaller, heavily abbreviated hand full of single-letter sigla separated by points (".ff.", "C.", "§", ".l.", ".j.", ".e."). On pieces 2, 5 and 6 the two sizes sit side by side on the same face. Red is used for paraph signs, for large pen-flourished initials, for one two-line rubric (piece 4) and for ruled red frames/boxes (pieces 2 and 6). There are small marginal signs and letters beside the text on piece 1.
Tentative interpretation only: a main text in the larger hand accompanied by a surrounding gloss or apparatus in the small hand, the small hand being dense with abbreviated references. I do not infer author, work, date or provenance. Whether all six pieces come from one book is not something the images settle: piece 4 is a cleaner, blacker hand than the rest and could be a different book.

WHAT I SELECTED AND WHAT REMAINS UNREAD
Selected: piece 2 face B (the only face with ten or more consecutive lines of legible small script, plus the larger column beside it); piece 6 face A (ten lines of the larger hand); piece 4 both faces (clear but only 2-8 letters per line); piece 5 face B right column (about sixteen short lines of small script); piece 1 face A line openings.
Left essentially unread because the surface is abraded, flaked or blank, not for want of looking: piece 3 face B (no writing visible at all), piece 6 face B (traces only), piece 5 face A (isolated words), piece 2 face A (isolated words), piece 1 face B and the lower half of piece 1 face A.
No span here is long enough to be called connected prose with confidence. Every line is cut at one or both ends. A wider view is not available in the packet; raking-light or multispectral images of piece 2 face A, piece 5 face A and piece 6 face B would be the useful addition.

Conventions: (..) proposed expansion; ? after an uncertain reading; [illegible] or [..] unreadable; [hole] physical loss; "/" between alternative readings of the same letters; ⁊ = Tironian et; § as written. Line numbers count from the top of the named image.

LIMITATIONS
- Every line on every piece is cropped at one end or both. I have not supplied any missing word or letter from sense.
- The request for several ten-line spans per face cannot be met by these leaves: only piece 2 face B (small-script block, 15 lines) and piece 6 face A (10 lines) reach that length, and both are cut and rubbed. Piece 4 gives 14 lines per face but only a few letters of each.
- Readings marked with ? are frequent and real. In the small hand, minims and the single-letter sigla are easily confused (u/n, c/t, f/s, l/i); the alternatives separated by "/" are of roughly equal weight unless one is listed first.
- I may have miscounted a line where a tile boundary or a hole falls; line numbers are for locating text in the named tile, not a claim about the original ruling.
- Column order across a piece (which column was read first) is not determinable from these scraps, and I cannot tell recto from verso.
- Whether the six pieces belong together is not established by the images.
- This is an unverified image reading.
